name: AgentSeed
tagline: A programming language for autonomous agents, where uncertainty, taint, cost and capability rules are checked at compile time.

audience.concern: Build agents whose safety rules are enforced by the compiler instead of added at runtime.
Read, check and reproduce what an agent is allowed to do before it runs.
Study an effect-tracked, type-safe language with a written specification and a conformance suite.

highlights.title: Effects must be discharged
highlights.text: Effectful operations return a Computation that has to be discharged before its value can be used.

highlights.title: Capabilities are signed tokens
highlights.text: Capability tokens are issued by the VM, signed with Ed25519, and can be attenuated and delegated.

highlights.title: Four grammar strata
highlights.text: S0 Seed for beginners and sandboxed agents, S1 Core for production, S2 Full with self-evolution hooks, S3 System for trusted orchestrators with human sign-off.

highlights.title: Provenance you can replay
highlights.text: Merkle-proofed, append-only logs support audit and deterministic replay.

highlights.title: Compiler and VM in Rust
highlights.text: seedc compiles .seed source to .aslb bytecode; seedvm runs it deterministically. MIT licensed, with a published conformance suite.

verifyIt: Run seed check on a program: the compiler type-checks it and verifies its effect, taint and contract rules without running it.

demo.title: Try the language
demo.summary: The in-browser compiler and VM are being built. Until then this page shows a labeled placeholder.

buildFromSource.title: Build from source
buildFromSource.intro: Build the seed command from source. Packaged installs are being confirmed.
buildFromSource.steps:
git clone https://github.com/agentseedlanguage-cpu/agentseed
cd agentseed
cargo build --release -p seedc-cli
./target/release/seed --version

faq.q: Which Rust version do I need?
faq.a: Rust 1.85 or newer. Run rustup update stable if the build complains about the version.

faq.q: What is the difference between seed check, run and build?
faq.a: seed check type-checks and verifies without producing output. seed run compiles and runs on the VM. seed build writes the .aslb bytecode file.
The project's own playground says in-browser compilation is coming soon. This site's Demo tab will use it when it exists.
